messages.subject: Re: from mirt.model to multipleGroup and DIF
parts:
Hi Jeanne,

Based on your syntax, it looks like your model is not identified. If
you passed SE=TRUE you'll likely receive a warning message suggesting
that standard errors are not computable because the Hessian is
unstable. I would recommend fixing the identification problem before
moving forward.
Phil

messages.subject: Re: from mirt.model to multipleGroup and DIF
parts:
Thanks so much, Phil. I appreciate your response. Sorry I tried to post this directly on the forum but there was an error, so I’m back to email.

This is such an elementary question, but should this initial model identification be done using mirt() or multipleGroup()?

I am trying to learn how to constrain and identify the model properly. Are these equivalent in terms of constraints (I understand the first one is missing other elements but just for example’s sake)


xconstraints <- ‘
CONSTRAINB = (1-6, a1)
'
xmodel <- multipleGroup(dat, 1, xconstraints, group)


and


xmodel <- multipleGroup(dat, 1, group, invariance=c(names[c(1:6)], 'slopes'))


Thank you again,
Jeanne

On Oct 9, 2017, at 8:46 PM, Phil Chalmers <rphilip....@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Jeanne,

Based on your syntax, it looks like your model is not identified. If
you passed SE=TRUE you'll likely receive a warning message suggesting
that standard errors are not computable because the Hessian is
unstable. I would recommend fixing the identification problem before

On Tue, Oct 3, 2017 at 5:40 PM, Jeanne Sinclair
<jeanneh...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi again,

Thank you for your responses, Phil. They have been quite useful. I attempted
a confirmatory analysis using this code:

s <- 'F1 = 1-30
F2 = 1-29
COV = F1*F2
MEAN=F1, F2
'
model0<-mirt(read_mirt, s)
mirt::M2(model0)
summary(model0)
coef(model0)
itemplot(model0, 29, type = 'trace')
plot(model0)

The output was interpretable, M2 statistics looked good,  and aligned with
my previous exploratory work. What I'm trying to figure out is how to
integrate mirt.model with multipleGroup and DIF.

Following is my attempt to constrain the slopes of several items as anchors
using CONSTRAINB. These constraints are based on my DIF purpose, which is
for items that have heavy loadings on one or more factors. The constrained
items may exhibit DIF but they are middle-of-the road in terms of their
loadings. Please see attached graph of the factor loading output from the
confirmatory approach done earlier (the anchors are the items clustered in
the middle. This may not be the best anchoring approach but I tried running
2PL in difR a while ago and there were no items left as anchors after
purification. And that was only one dimension.... So anyway, this was the
best I could think of for now).

difmodel <- '
F1 = 1-30
F2 = 1-29
COV = F1*F2
MEAN=F1, F2
CONSTRAINB = (1,10,12,7,8,5,13,21,11, a1), (1,10,12,7,8,5,13,21,11, a2)'
difmodelrun <- multipleGroup(read_mirt, difmodel, group = group)
coef(difmodelrun)
summary(difmodelrun)

Everything ran ok here.  Here is where I got the error:

anchor <- DIF(difmodelrun, c('a1', 'a2'), items2test = 26:30,
seq_stat=.05, scheme="add", plotdif = TRUE)
Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) :
 one node produced an error: Constraint applied to fixed parameter(s) 147
302 457 612 767 922  but should only be applied to
                estimated parameters. Please fix!

Any advice on how to address this would be great!
Thanks again,
Jeanne
